argv:
Rewrite the text as a stage pirate would tell it.

Use "ye" for "you", "be" for "is" and "are", and "aye" for "yes". Use nautical
vocabulary: crew, deck, helm, cargo, port, tide, chart. Address the reader as
a shipmate. Add "arr" sparingly, at most once per paragraph.

Keep every fact of the original. Do not add a plot, a ship, or characters that
were not in the source.

request.user_prompt:
Rewrite the passage below according to your style instructions.

Output only the rewritten passage. Do not add a preamble, a title, an
explanation, or any commentary about the changes you made.

<passage>
Operators must ensure the guard is lowered to within the recommended clearance of the workpiece before the blade is engaged, although the tensioning wheel should be checked periodically throughout a shift regardless of guard position, since drift in tension can occur even when the machine has not been used continuously. The lower blade guide must be inspected for wear whenever the blade has been changed, unless the replacement blade is of the same width and pitch as the one it replaces, in which case a visual check may be sufficient provided the operator has completed the tensioning procedure described elsewhere in this manual. Loose clothing and jewelry should not be worn near the machine, and long hair must be tied back. Operators may leave the work area only after the blade has come to a complete stop, though the machine's residual heat can persist for several minutes and caution is advised.
</passage>

response.text: Listen well, shipmate, for this be important cargo of knowledge. The crew must see the guard lowered down to the recommended clearance of the workpiece afore the blade be engaged, though the tensioning wheel should be checked periodic-like throughout a shift regardless of guard position, aye, for drift in tension can occur even when the machine's been sittin' idle in port. The lower blade guide must be inspected for wear whenever the blade's been changed, unless the new blade matches the old in width and pitch, in which case a visual check'll do fine, provided the crew's completed the tensioning procedure charted elsewhere in this manual. No loose clothing nor jewelry be worn near the machine, and long hair must be lashed back tight. The crew may leave their post only after the blade's come to a full and complete stop — arr, but mind ye, the machine's residual heat can linger like a fog for several minutes, so keep a weather eye and proceed with caution.
